Analyst
-------
  [critical] Blue lost R4 on a broken buy: the loss bonus had escalated far enough to fund a real buy, but the team still walked in on a force.
           rule: analyst.pivotal_broken_buy, 5 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue went into the pivotal R4 already 2 rounds into a losing streak -- the round that decided the match was played on bonus money.
           rule: analyst.pivotal_streak, 4 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue was simply out-fought in the pivotal R4, taking only 0% of the round's kills (sim-approx: kill share stands in for real trade windows).
           rule: analyst.pivotal_trade_collapse, 4 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue got the spike down but could not hold it -- only 33% of its plants converted into round wins.
           rule: analyst.post_plant_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue was out-traded across the match, taking 36% of round kills over 18 rounds against a 50% even split (sim-approx: kill share stands in for real trade windows).
           rule: analyst.trade_efficiency, 18 feature row(s) cited
  [info] R4 was the match's pivotal round -- the largest single swing (0.110) in the win-probability proxy. Red took it, Blue lost it.
           rule: analyst.pivotal_round, 4 feature row(s) cited

Economist
---------
  [critical] Blue broke its buy 6 times (R2, R3, R4, R6, R9, R17) -- rounds where the escalated loss bonus should have funded a real buy and the team went in short anyway.
           rule: economist.broken_buy_count, 6 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue force-bought 4 rounds back to back (R1, R2, R3, R4). One force is a read; a run this long means the team never got off the back foot long enough to rebuild.
           rule: economist.consecutive_force, 4 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue force-bought in 10 of 18 rounds (56%), past the 30% mark where forcing stops being a read and starts being a habit.
           rule: economist.force_buy_frequency, 18 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Blue stole 0 of its 1 eco rounds (0%).
           rule: economist.eco_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Red stole 1 of its 1 eco rounds (100%).
           rule: economist.eco_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited

provenance.detail: val-match-v1 requires a Riot production key. Matches here are generated by an in-repo simulator that emits payloads in the documented val-match-v1 shape, grounded in real agent and map UUIDs fetched live from val-content-v1. Nothing is scraped and no unofficial API is used. Every module downstream of the match adapter is source-agnostic, so live data swaps in with no code change.
provenance.note: Simulated data conforming to the val-match-v1 schema — production key application pending
provenance.proxy_note: Momentum index, not a calibrated win probability: a bounded logistic over score state and round spend differential. It ranks rounds against each other within one match and says nothing about the odds of winning.
provenance.sim_approx_note: Kill share stands in for trade efficiency: the simulator emits no death timestamps, so real trade windows cannot be detected.
